summary.headline: Sundrop Brands Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR463 crore, with normalized EBITDA margin up 240 bps.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 21% YoY to a run rate of INR463 crore, with H1 revenue at INR891 crore (up 18%). Normalized EBITDA margin expanded 240 bps; on an unadjusted basis the expansion was 370 bps because prior-year one-off project expenses were absent this year. Growth was led by ACT II popcorn ready-to-eat, e-commerce (up about 43%, now 19% of sales) and Italian pasta, while peanut butter stabilised but remained weak in volume. Operating cash flow was negative in H1 (about INR49-50 crore per the analyst), which management attributed to deliberate inventory build in corn and oats plus receivables rising with sales.

financial_highlights.change: Edible oil margin diluted; overall margin up about 20 bps

financial_highlights.value: Close to INR90 crore, 19% of company sales

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow (H1, as cited by analyst)

segments.name: Sundrop (core brand)
segments.commentary: Grew 19% in Q2 and 17% in H1. Management says core portfolio volume growth is about 10-12%, with value growth of about 18%.

segments.name: Del Monte
segments.commentary: Grew 26% in Q2 and 20% in H1. Italian pasta volume grew about 33% in Q2 (about 25-26% normalized, per management); olive oil volume grew about 15%.

segments.name: ACT II popcorn
segments.commentary: Ready-to-eat grew 38% in value and 23% in volume in Q2; ready-to-cook grew about 12% in value and 5-6% in volume. Blended franchise volume is about 10-11%.

segments.name: Edible oil
segments.commentary: Q2 volume grew about 5% and value about 19%, with a target of 4-5% volume growth. Margins are being protected rather than expanded.

segments.name: Peanut butter (spreads)
segments.commentary: Value stabilised and volume still under pressure. Decline rate improved from -8% in Q4 to -3% in Q1 to about -1% in Q2. E-commerce growth is about 18%.

segments.name: Culinary (ketchup, mayo, dips, pasta sauces)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume grew 13% (H1 11%) and value grew 21% in Q2 (H1 18%).

guidance_outlook: Management expects volume growth to stay around 10-11% for the portfolio, with about 3-4% from premiumisation and 6-7% from price increases (value growth is driven by price).
Edible oil volume target of 4-5% growth, with margins protected rather than expanded. Foods is expected to drive margin expansion.
Olive oil volume growth expected at about 12-15% in Q3; pasta momentum expected to continue into the festive season.
Peanut butter e-commerce growth targeted to move ahead of category growth within two quarters; entry into modern trade and general trade targeted for FY28.
Working capital: management expects inventory and receivable levels to normalise in Q3 as uncertainty stabilises.
Price increases in Del Monte annual export and key-account contracts are expected mainly in Q4 (December to March renewals), not Q1.
No significant input-cost-led margin impact or further price increase expected in the coming quarter; popcorn corn contracts for next year are secured with no significant inflation expected.
Management says it does not see an inflationary environment in the next 3-4 months, with recent edible oil moves in the range of plus or minus 5%.
capex_capacity: Growth model is shifting to capital-efficient use of third-party (3P) manufacturing sites alongside existing plants; management did not give capex amounts or capacity figures.
Popcorn sourcing is diversified: indirect contract farming with Indian growers in Andhra Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, with harvest by February, plus imported varieties for microwave packs.
Sales Force Automation completed; about 400,000 outlets directly covered, with about 80% of outlets ordering regularly in Q2 FY27.
24 new products launched in Q2 and about 120+ over the last two years; about 6% of sales come from NPDs launched in the last two years.
Advertising-to-sales ratio on core categories is about 9%, against a stated target of 9-10%, up from about 4-5% historically. Core categories are about 60-63% of the portfolio.
demand_pricing: Pricing: broad-based inflation in packaging and edible oil was passed to consumers through calibrated price increases. Price contributed about 6-7% to growth.
Edible oil pricing is calibrated to keep premium staples stable. Government cut edible oil duty in September, and management says the benefit was partly passed on.
E-commerce growth of 43% is driven by performance marketing, tech capability and upgrades to larger packs. The channel is growing about 18-25% overall, per management.
Quick commerce is a structural tailwind for snacking and impulse consumption, which is helping ACT II RTE growth.
General trade is expected to grow more slowly than e-commerce, modern trade and quick commerce, though sales force automation is improving ROI there.
Culinary export business in Southeast Asia is growing with new product introductions, and B2B key-account penetration is increasing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ready-to-cook volume growth in ACT II, and is e-commerce driving the popcorn volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: RTC volume grew about 5-6% and the blended popcorn franchise about 10-11%. E-commerce is upgrading consumers to larger packs; RTE large-pack growth was about 53% against 23% for small packs, for a blended RTE growth of about 37%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is peanut butter losing share, and what is the plan to win it back?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium value-added variants (chocolate, high-protein, zero-separation) rose from 8.3% of saliency in Q1 to 12.4% in Q2. Decline has narrowed to about -1% in Q2. The e-commerce target is to grow ahead of category within two quarters, with modern trade entry in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was operating cash flow negative in H1, and will Q3 turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to deliberate inventory build in corn and oats for supply security, plus receivables rising with sales. DSOs were stable. Management expects levels to normalise in Q3 as uncertainty eases.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Italian volume growth jump to 30%, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Pasta volume grew about 33% and olive oil about 15%. Part of the jump is from a weak base after the September GST change; normalised pasta growth is about 25-26%. Olive oil growth is guided at 12-15% for Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of core versus non-core growth, and is the trend continuing?
qa_highlights.answer: Core volume is growing about 12%, against 10% previously, and is about 2x non-core volume. Edible oil value grew about 15% on volume of about 5%. Core value growth is about 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin outlook and do you need further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no major input-cost pressure in the next quarter. Del Monte export and key-account contracts will be repriced mainly in Q4, which should help margins from then.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 21% growth split between volume, innovation and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume is about 10%, innovation and premiumisation add about 3-4%, and price increases add about 6-7%.

risks_watch: Negative H1 operating cash flow driven by inventory build and receivables; Q3 normalisation needs to be confirmed.
Peanut butter volume is still declining (about -1% in Q2), and the premium variants are only 12.4% of saliency. Recovery depends on e-commerce momentum moving into general trade and modern trade.
Edible oil margin is being protected rather than expanded. Commodity volatility of plus or minus 5% is manageable, but the outlook could change.
Advertising spend is down YoY in the quarter (management says it is up sequentially). Competitive intensity in spreads is rising.
E-commerce growth (43%) may not hold through the festive season, and quick commerce pricing and competition could affect it.
Del Monte price increases depend on contract renewals in December to March, so the benefit lands mainly in Q4.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth momentum and margins, with a clear focus on ROI-led marketing. Management was more guarded on peanut butter volume, edible oil margins and the timing of working capital normalisation. Some answers were long and repeated points, and the quantitative breakdown of cash flow was less precise than analysts wanted.
key_quotes: Our revenue grew by 21% year-on-year in Q2, which is supported with a very strong and healthy momentum of growth across our core categories and across our emerging channels.
In Edible Oil business, our strategy has been more calibrated increasing to keep our pricing premium stable constant.
So I would say a real way to look is to read this number is about 10% volume, 3% premiumization and 6% to 7% impact is coming on account of price increases.
Today, we have reached about 18% growth. Our ambition will be within next 2 quarters to put it ahead of category growth in e-commerce channel.

growth.why: Management guides portfolio volume growth of about 10-11% plus 6-7% price (value growth ~16-18%), backed by demand gains in ACT II RTE, e-commerce and Italian pasta, but with no quantified capacity additions, capex amounts, or new order book; 3P-manufacturing shift lacks figures.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Normalized EBITDA margin up 240 bps in Q2 with Foods driving expansion, and Del Monte export/key-account price increases land mainly in Q4 (Dec-Mar renewals), though edible oil margins are only being protected and no input-cost pressure is seen next quarter.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capex amounts or capacity figures given; growth is shifting to capital-efficient third-party manufacturing, and modern and general trade entry for peanut butter is targeted for FY28, but no utilisation or plant additions were disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides portfolio volume growth of about 10-11% (3-4% premiumisation plus price-independent core volume ~12%), olive oil guided at 12-15% in Q3, and edible oil at 4-5%, though peanut butter volume is still about -1% in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; no utilisation level was disclosed, so the case for a new capex announcement cannot be read from this call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Growth of 21% in Q2 and 18% in H1 is running ahead of the ~10-11% volume plus 6-7% price framework, but management did not raise guidance and volume remains guided at 10-11%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was negative (about INR49-50 crore) and working capital normalisation in Q3 is not yet confirmed, while peanut butter volume remains at about -1% and e-commerce at 43% may not hold through the festive season.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 24 new products launched in Q2 and about 120+ over two years, with NPDs at about 6% of sales; premium peanut butter variants rose to 12.4% of saliency and Culinary export is adding new product introductions.

rows.label: Inventory and receivables normalise in Q3
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was about negative INR49-50 crore from corn/oats inventory build and receivables rising with sales; management expects normalisation in Q3 but gave no figures.

rows.label: Del Monte export and key-account repricing
rows.why: Price increases in annual export and key-account contracts are expected mainly in Q4, as December to March renewals come up, so the benefit lands after the next quarter.

rows.label: Peanut butter volume recovery
rows.why: Decline narrowed from -8% in Q4 to -3% in Q1 and about -1% in Q2, with e-commerce targeted to grow ahead of category within two quarters, but volume is still negative.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth momentum, margins and ROI-led marketing, but guarded on peanut butter volume, edible oil margins and working capital timing; analysts pressed on the cash flow breakdown and the sustainability of the Italian pasta jump.
